$comment: Authoring input for `npm run sprites:emotions`. Nothing here ships to the browser — it
is the prompt book for the Ludo.ai generator, and the record of what each clip was asked
to be, so a re-run reproduces the same intent.
Prompt rules learned the hard way, keep to them:
- Describe POSTURE, not expression. A Trial sprite's face is 50-80px on screen; a raised
eyebrow is invisible and asking for one just wastes the model's attention.
- Say 'in place', 'no travel'. Left unsaid, the model walks the animal out of frame and
the clip cannot loop against a static stage slot.
- Framing comes from each animal's `view`, never from the prompt text: the cast is NOT
uniformly side-on. The owl is drawn front-facing and the raccoon's sitting pose is a
three-quarter — telling either of them 'side view, facing left' asks the generator to
turn the character, and the clip then will not cut against its own idle loop.
- Keep the silhouette. The reference frame carries the character; the prompt should only
ever move it.
- Never name a posture the animal has to CHANGE STATE to reach. 'Crouched low' made the
generator lie the donkey down over the clip and never stand it back up: a transition,
not a held attitude, and one that cannot loop. Say what the body does while it stays
where it is, and say outright what it must not do ('never lies down').
- Watch the height swing in the review output. The runtime scales a clip off one union
bounding box, so a character whose height wanders 20%+ across frames renders too small
for most of the clip however good it looks in isolation.

talking.prompt: {view}. The {species} stays in place and talks: head bobbing gently in time with speech, mouth opening and closing, body relaxed and weight even. Small, steady, conversational. Seamless loop, no travel, same silhouette throughout.

doubtful.prompt: {view}. The {species} stays in place and reacts with skepticism: weight shifting back away from the listener, head drawing back and tilting slightly, a slow doubtful shake of the head. Unconvinced, guarded. Seamless loop, no travel, same silhouette throughout.

angry.prompt: {view}. The {species} stays in place and is angry: weight driving forward, head lowered and thrust toward the target, body tensed and shoulders squared, sharp agitated movement. Seamless loop, no travel, same silhouette throughout.

thinking.prompt: {view}. The {species} stays in place and thinks: nearly still, head lowered and turned slightly away, a slow considering nod, weight settled. Quiet and deliberate. Seamless loop, no travel, same silhouette throughout.

sneaky.prompt: {view}. The {species} stays standing on all fours the entire time and speaks conspiratorially: head craned forward and dipped toward the listener, ears flattening back, eyes flicking sideways mid-sentence. Sly, secretive, up to something. It never lies down, never sits, never lowers its body. Starts and ends in the exact pose of the reference image. Seamless loop, no travel, same silhouette throughout.

fox.$comment: A fox carries emotion in two places the donkey does not: pointed EARS (upright, swivelled, pinned flat back) and a big bushy TAIL. Both are silhouette elements with real visual weight, so they read at stage scale where a muzzle alone would not — this is the quadruped equivalent of leading the owl with its eyes. Every override also pins the feet positively ('stay planted exactly where they are and never move') rather than only saying 'no travel', because that is the phrasing that finally stopped the owl flaring its wings.

talking.prompt: {view}. The red fox stands in place on all fours and talks: its muzzle opens and closes with each phrase, its head bobs gently in time, its ears stay upright and flick once, and the tip of its bushy tail sways slowly. All four feet stay planted exactly where they are in the reference image and never move. Seamless loop, no travel, same silhouette throughout.

doubtful.prompt: {view}. The red fox stands in place on all fours and is unconvinced: its head draws back and tilts, one upright ear swivels back and returns, its muzzle stays closed, and its bushy tail hangs still. All four feet stay planted exactly where they are in the reference image and never move; the body stays standing the whole time. Guarded and skeptical. Seamless loop, no travel, same silhouette throughout.

angry.prompt: {view}. The red fox stands in place on all fours, ears flattened hard back against its skull for the whole clip, muzzle wrinkled open in a snarl showing teeth, head lowered until it is level with its shoulders and pushed toward the target, and its low bushy tail lashing from side to side. All four feet stay planted exactly where they are in the reference image and never move — it does not step, lunge, walk or pounce, and the body stays standing. Seamless loop, no travel, same silhouette throughout.

thinking.prompt: {view}. The red fox stands in place on all fours and considers something: nearly still, its head lowered and turned slightly away, its ears rotating slowly back and forward again, its muzzle closed, its bushy tail hanging still. All four feet stay planted exactly where they are in the reference image and never move. Quiet and deliberate. Seamless loop, no travel, same silhouette throughout.

sneaky.prompt: {view}. The red fox stands in place on all fours and speaks conspiratorially: its head lowers and cranes slowly forward toward the listener, its ears tilt back, and its eyes flick sideways. Its big bushy tail stays whole and fully drawn for every frame, held low and curled behind it, the same full shape and length as in the reference image. The movement is ONE slow continuous glide from start to finish — gentle and unhurried, with no sudden jumps, no fast beats and no snapping back. All four feet stay planted exactly where they are in the reference image and never move; it stays standing the whole time and never crouches flat, never lies down, never sits. Sly and secretive. Starts and ends in the exact pose of the reference image. Seamless loop, no travel, same silhouette throughout.

raccoon.$comment: Staged sitting up on the Trial stand (`idleTrial`), so the reference is the sitting pose, not the four-legged crouch — an emotion clip generated from the crouch would pop the moment the debate cuts to it.

angry.prompt: {view}. The raccoon stays sitting upright in place and is angry: chest thrust forward, head lowered and jabbing toward the target, forepaws gesturing sharply. Seamless loop, no travel, same silhouette throughout.

sneaky.prompt: {view}. The raccoon stays sitting upright in place and speaks conspiratorially: hunching down over its forepaws, head dipped and craned forward, glancing furtively to the side. Sly and secretive. Seamless loop, no travel, same silhouette throughout.

owl.$comment: A standing bird has no gait and no shoulders to square, so the generic four-legged posture prompts read as nonsense here. Two hazards this body has and the quadrupeds do not — it can TAKE OFF, and the word 'perch' invites a branch the source art does not contain — so every prompt forbids both. Its angry clip took five attempts: forbidding the wing flare never worked (an 'angry bird' prior outweighs any 'never spread' instruction) and only freezing the body positively did — 'body, wings and feet stay exactly as in the reference, ONLY THE FACE MOVES'. AND THE BIG ONE: this owl breaks the global 'posture, not expression' rule. Its eyes are ~40% of its body area in high-contrast yellow, so the face IS the silhouette and reads fine at stage scale. The first pass proved it — a body-posture 'angry' read as a surprised owl talking, while 'sneaky' asking for narrowed eyes was the best clip generated for any animal. Lead the owl's emotions with eyes, brow and beak.

talking.prompt: {view}. The owl stays standing in place on its own two feet and talks: beak opening and closing, head bobbing slightly with each phrase, body still and upright. It never takes off and never leaves the ground; no perch or branch appears. Seamless loop, no travel, same silhouette throughout.

doubtful.prompt: {view}. The owl stays standing in place on its own two feet and is skeptical: weight settling back, head rotating slowly to one side and tilting, a long unimpressed stare, one slow blink. It stays upright the whole time and never takes off. Seamless loop, no travel, same silhouette throughout.

angry.prompt: {view}. A close, still shot of the owl. Its body, wings, feet and outline stay exactly as they are in the reference image and do not move at all — the wings remain tucked down at its sides in the same shape as the reference in every frame. ONLY THE FACE MOVES. The brow feathers press down into a hard V over the eyes, each big yellow eye narrows into a slanted slit with the bright yellow still visible, and the beak opens and snaps shut in a sharp scolding. The head tips forward a little toward the viewer and back. Nothing else in the picture changes. Starts and ends in the exact pose of the reference image. Seamless loop, no travel, same silhouette throughout.

thinking.prompt: {view}. The owl stays standing in place on its own two feet and thinks: almost motionless, head turning slowly to one side and back, a single slow blink. It stays upright and never takes off. Seamless loop, no travel, same silhouette throughout.

sneaky.prompt: {view}. The owl stays standing upright in place on its own two feet and speaks conspiratorially: head craned forward and dipped toward the listener, rotating to glance furtively to one side and back, eyes narrowing, body still. It never crouches, never hunches its body down, never lies down, never takes off. Sly and secretive. Starts and ends in the exact pose of the reference image. Seamless loop, no travel, same silhouette throughout.
